name: a future offset in an as_of_month_day year_offset range contributes NULL rather than today's value (executed-result parity)
description: year_axis_month_day_boundary has TWO call sites -- the year-axis join and the bespoke main_select_string_year_offset_range, which emits its own correlated subquery per offset. Removing the future clamp changes both, and the range path is the one no other fixture exercises against a future anchor: keeptradecut-as-of-month-day-year-offset-range-result-equivalence.json uses year 2023 with offsets [0,1], so both of its boundaries are in the past and it is green either way. Requests as_of_month_day 03-01 on year 2025 with year_offset [0,30], so the two per-offset boundaries are 2025-03-01 and 2055-03-01. Only the first can resolve: the seeded 2025-02-25 observation sits inside its (2025-01-30, 2025-03-01] window, and no observation exists near 2055. The 2055 arm therefore contributes NULL, which AVG SKIPS, so the average is 1000 rather than being dragged toward another value. The now() - interval '5 days' seed at 4000 is what makes the clamp mutation falsifiable: re-add the outer LEAST(..., now()) and the 2055 boundary collapses to now, the second arm resolves 4000, and AVG returns 2500 instead of 1000. The 2025-09-15 decoy at 9999 lies outside every window and keeps the reference_sql threshold honest.
